episodes.title: Why the AI World Will Never Be the Same
episodes.about: Until this week, Jensen Huang was one of the most powerful people in the most powerful industry on earth. Now, after 33 years running Nvidia, he is out. Ahead of the show's usual Friday conversation, Kevin Roose delivers a personal essay: he has spent years covering the race to AGI and nearly made Huang a main character in his book. He explains the three central roles Huang played in the AI boom, and why he thinks the affairs alone do not explain why Huang had to go. A note added after recording: Reuters reported that Huang allegedly had a third affair, with a second Nvidia employee.
episodes.why: Always-include show: a 19-minute solo essay from Kevin - the three roles Huang played in the AI boom, and why he thinks the affairs alone do not explain why Huang had to go.

episodes.title: Every Day Is Zero Day | Wiz CTO Ami Luttwak
episodes.about: AI is not just helping defenders find vulnerabilities. It is giving attackers the speed and expertise to exploit them faster than many companies can respond. Wiz co-founder and CTO Ami Luttwak joins a16z General Partners Zane Lackey and Sarah Wang to unpack what he calls 'Black October,' a wave of vulnerabilities and agentic attacks that he believes marks a turning point for cybersecurity. They break down PHP2Shell, why AI is collapsing the time between vulnerability discovery and exploitation, and what happens when open-source models put increasingly sophisticated offensive capabilities in more hands. Luttwak argues companies need to continuously attack their own systems, automate investigation and patching, and design infrastructure assuming sophisticated attackers will get in: if attackers can move in minutes, defenders can no longer operate on human timelines.
episodes.why: Out today: Wiz CTO Ami Luttwak on 'Black October' - AI collapsing the time between a vulnerability appearing and attackers exploiting it, down to minutes.

episodes.title: Powering AI-Driven Drug Discovery with President of Isomorphic Labs Max Jaderberg
episodes.about: Drug discovery and development has long relied on expensive, time-consuming empirical trial and error. By shifting the discovery process onto computers, Isomorphic Labs wants to fundamentally change medicine from a process of discovery to one of precision engineering. Elad Gil sits down with Isomorphic's president Max Jaderberg to discuss his vision for using predictive AI models to achieve experimental accuracy. Jaderberg details how AlphaFold provided the first proof of concept that a deep learning model could generalize in biology, how a model's compounding of learnings increases the probability of success and speed in real-world clinical trials, evolving past the need for animal testing through in-silico models, drug design engines that are agnostic of disease area, target class and modality, and why accurate molecule engineering unlocks multidrug cocktails that span complex biological pathways.
episodes.why: Isomorphic Labs president Max Jaderberg on turning drug discovery from trial-and-error into engineering: models accurate enough to predict experiments, and a path past animal testing.

episodes.title: AI could help hospitals diagnose PTSD in real time
episodes.about: Every year, millions of people in the United States develop PTSD from a traumatic event - like a car crash, an assault or a freak accident. Many of those people end up in the ER answering the same question: 'What brought you to the emergency department today?' Now, a research team in New York has an AI model that can use patients' answers and demographics to produce one number that tells medical staff how likely a patient is to develop PTSD a month later. The work, published in the journal Nature Communications, could help an often-overloaded emergency department team prevent mental health disorders before they start.
episodes.why: Twelve minutes, out today: a New York team's model reads ER patients' own answers and gives staff one number - how likely that patient is to develop PTSD a month later.

episodes.title: #251: Forward-Deployed Engineers, Shadow AI, the Owner Bottleneck, AI on Your Resume & Token Budgets
episodes.about: Paul Roetzer and Cathy McPhillips answer 14 questions from their Scaling AI and Intro to AI classes: scaling AI under SOC 2 and HIPAA, whether companies should block frontier models and only allow self-hosted AI, what AI teams should prioritize when governance is not ready for agents, how much platform standardization organizations need and how leaders should handle shadow AI, where forward-deployed engineers fit and who owns AI enablement, how business owners can use AI to become less of a bottleneck, what responsible AI personalization looks like, how to show AI skills to a hiring manager, whether AI will ever write as creatively as a talented human, and whether top performers will negotiate token budgets into job offers.
episodes.why: Discovery pick - a weekly show where AI consultants answer business users' real questions, new here: shadow AI, who owns agent rollouts, and token budgets showing up in job offers.
